correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed using D W_T=[UY]_0^T−∫Y dV, where Y and V are the centered states. With c=E[YV]=s²/(κ+Γ), the Poisson solution for Γ(YV−c) is ψ=(Γ(YV−c)+hV)/(κ+Γ). Combining its martingale with −∫Y dM^V gives the Brownian coefficient √(2/D) ΓV/(κ+Γ) and jump (h−κY)ΔV/[D(κ+Γ)]. Since q_v(ΔV)²=Γ(2s²+hv), insertion of E[Y²]=(D+c)/κ and E[Y²V]=2hc/(2κ+Γ) gives exactly the stated variance. Stationarity gives an O(1) L² endpoint and hence a vanishing scaled endpoint covariance; ergodicity gives bracket convergence, and bounded switching rates plus E[(1+|Y|)^4]<∞ bound the expected normalized jump Lindeberg term by O(1/T) at fixed cutoff. Differentiation reduces the peak criterion to comparing 2h²/s² with G(t), which decreases from 1 to 0 on [0,1]. Solving 2(r−1)²<r gives 1/2<r<2, with strict decrease for positive stiffness at both endpoints and the symmetric peak at Γ. The free limit is one-sided, not an unconfined stationary law.
residual_risks: The packaged Monte Carlo starts the position at zero and is not an exact finite-time stationary test. No simulation or formal certificate is needed for the analytic result. The observable excludes any separate internal-state entropy contribution.

value.rationale: A sharp, speed- and temperature-independent distinction separates monotone confinement response from a strict finite-stiffness maximum. The variance is a natural statistic of the same active work whose mean was known; the competing stiffness terms and exact boundary rates are useful beyond merely invoking a CLT.
residual_risks: Value is confined to the stated active-work observable and the two-state harmonic model.
